requirements.exactText: [PES-DIA-0047] MUST cap ordinary nonfatal active conditions at 9999 and reserve the 10000th slot for at most one fatal runtime/invariant condition. Before accepting a typed command or provider transition, the runtime shall calculate its complete post-boundary active-condition set; admission requires both nonfatal count <= 9999 and total count <= 10000. A violating command or rejectable provider transition is rejected wholly before its causal mutation commits and appends EDU-DIA-0002 with the command/transition ID, proposed counts, and deterministically ordered proposed ConditionKeys. A non-rejectable execution-derived nonfatal transition that would violate admission, including counter saturation detected during an executing scan, is not inserted; it instead activates EDU-RTM-0006 in the reserved slot with the suppressed ConditionKey/cause and enters FAULTED before normal output commit. The first ordinary internally generated fatal condition may likewise occupy the reserved slot and apply its declared CPU response; a second condition is not evaluated after the fatal boundary. Any path that bypasses admission applies the same invariant-failure rule. Once 10000 conditions are active, only actions that acknowledge, clear, reset, or otherwise reduce/resolve existing conditions may be admitted until capacity is available.

requirements.exactText: [PES-DIA-0048] MUST retain at most 100000 diagnostic records per controller as one optional EVENT_GAP compaction sentinel followed by the newest immutable causal event suffix. Before appending an event that would exceed capacity, evict the oldest causal records necessary to retain the incoming event and one sentinel, then create or extend the single sentinel to cover every evicted record from the first through last canonical `(UniverseEpoch, controllerEpoch, eventSequence, OccurrenceId)` key and an exact lost-record count. The sentinel is derived buffer metadata, has the GapId defined byte-for-byte by PES-DIA-0051, and is excluded from causal event sequencing/acknowledgement. Within one continuous live timeline between explicit timeline replacements, its lost range/count may change only by monotonic extension; an ordinary controllerEpoch/ReplaySegment change does not relax that rule. Its compacted-reference summary set is recomputed exactly under PES-DIA-0049 as the retained suffix changes. Snapshot restore installs the captured sentinel and retained suffix byte-for-byte as the initial diagnostic state of the new UniverseEpoch before the new segment's restore event is appended; that explicit timeline replacement may therefore reduce or replace the pre-restore live sentinel. Boundary event batches compact one event at a time in PES-DIA-0028 order; the newest incoming event is always retained. Snapshot and replay shall reproduce byte-identical sentinel content and retained suffix.

requirements.exactText: [PES-DIA-0049] MUST preserve an evicted event that remains a direct parent or root of any retained event as `COMPACTED { OccurrenceId, codeVersion, lifecycle, primaryTargetId?, canonicalOrderKey }` inside the EVENT_GAP sentinel, ordered by canonicalOrderKey then OccurrenceId. Retained causal edges continue to name the original OccurrenceId and mark resolution state COMPACTED; the summary is valid only when canonicalOrderKey falls inside the sentinel's lost range. The sentinel contains exactly the distinct still-referenced evicted parent/root summaries, removes a summary when no retained event references it, and caps the set at two summaries per retained causal event. It shall never invent prose, acknowledgement, recovery, value, or source data absent from the original event.

requirements.exactText: [PES-DIA-0050] MUST use OccurrenceId as the sole diagnostic causal-graph identity. A causal root event has `parentOccurrenceId = null` and `rootOccurrenceId = its own OccurrenceId`; that equality is a root label, not a graph edge. Every caused event names at most one direct parentOccurrenceId and copies that parent's rootOccurrenceId. A continuing condition's INCOMING event is the condition episode's root unless an upstream event caused it; ACKNOWLEDGED and CLEARED keep that same root. ConditionId identifies the active episode and shall never occupy either occurrence field. `RootOccurrenceId` is the typed role of the rootOccurrenceId field and of all trace root filters.

requirements.exactText: [PES-DIA-0051] MUST construct every PES-DIA UUIDv5 name with `DIA-ID-TLV-1`: prefix ASCII bytes `PES-DIA-ID-TLV-1` plus NUL, followed by one recursively encoded tuple. Each value is one ASCII type tag plus a four-byte unsigned big-endian payload length plus payload: `U` = 16 RFC-4122 network-order UUID bytes; `N` = exactly eight unsigned big-endian integer bytes; `S` = NFC-normalized UTF-8 string; `E` = uppercase ASCII enum token; `H` = exactly 32 hash bytes; `T` = concatenated encoded members in declared order; `Z` = null with zero length. ConditionKeyHash is SHA-256 of a `T` containing codeVersion; provider U/Z; primary-target kind plus UUID or ordered member-UUID path; and each registry discriminator as `(name, TypeId, SHA-256 of its PES-SNP-0017 canonical typed-value bytes)` in registry order. GapId fields are `(GAP, UniverseId, VirtualControllerId, EDU-DIA-0001 version, firstLost UniverseEpoch, controllerEpoch, eventSequence, OccurrenceId)`. No delimiter text, locale formatting, host endianness, unordered map, or alternative UUID string representation enters these name bytes.

rows: Record the actual accepted Phase 1 HEAD/tag; confirm clean or intentionally accounted state; run the documented closure/local gate and clean build/test/launch once; create the Phase 2 start checkpoint.
Existing closure gate passes. If the report omitted evidence but the repository gate passes, record that fact and proceed; do not reopen Phase 1.

Canonical project kernel, UUID graph, typed commands/events, dependencies, tombstones, copy/move/rename/delete, transactional undo/redo, dirty/build state, and simulator-native persistence/recovery/migration.
Real UI can create, save, reopen, rename, delete, undo, and copy while identity/reference invariants and round-trip tests pass.
Functional engineering workbench: home/new/open, project navigator, tabbed work area, contextual properties, build/diagnostic pane, status surfaces, keyboard basics, and synchronized selection.
UI actions mutate/query canonical domain state; no production mock or UI-owned truth remains.

EDU-21 TrainingProfile, fictional controller/module catalog, racks/slots/channels, address allocator, data-only VirtualNetwork, tags, constants, canonical types, symbol resolution, and cross references.
Valid configurations build; illegal slots, duplicate names/addresses, overlaps, and unsafe virtual-address inputs produce real diagnostics and zero host-network activity.
OB/FC/FB/DB program model, interfaces, instances, call/dependency graph, instruction registry, state ownership, and invalidation.
Interface changes invalidate real callers; recursion/alias/state errors block artifacts; instance independence is proven.
Compiler pipeline, BuildAttempt/BuildReport/BuildArtifact, verified typed IR, source maps, probes, diagnostic registry, and an initial runnable SCL vertical slice through the production runtime.
A nontrivial SCL project compiles, loads, runs, monitors, and fails honestly on invalid syntax/types without eval or a separate runtime.
Semantic LAD editor and lowering: networks, contacts, coils, branches, boxes, calls, stateful instructions, structural legality, editing operations, and live probe mapping.
LAD executes by semantic graph, never coordinates; malformed graphs remain editable but emit no executable IR.
Typed-port FBD editor/lowering and completion of the SCL language-service baseline; all languages share resolver, types, instructions, compiler, IR, diagnostics, and runtime.
Mixed-language calls and equivalence corpora pass; no per-language semantic engine exists.

Deterministic VirtualController, CPU modes, virtual time, process images, memory/retention/reset, timers/counters/edges, runtime faults, snapshots/replay, and typed raw-input/output VirtualIOBoundary bench.

normativeRecords.exactText: The following registry is the complete EDU-21 Core 1.0 baseline. `T` means one exact canonical type, `N` one exact integer or floating type, `I` one exact integer type, `S` one exact signed integer type, `B` one exact bit-string type, and `A<T>` one exact-shape fixed ARRAY. Each listed stable ID is one unique generic InstructionDefinition family whose constraints admit the stated type bindings. A successful binding creates a deterministic InstructionInstantiationId as SHA-256 over canonical `{familyId, orderedBoundTypeIds}`; it is not a second registry definition and does not weaken family-ID uniqueness. Slash abbreviations repeat the unchanged prefix and `.v1` suffix: for example, `EDU.BOOL.AND.v1 / OR / XOR` means the three exact family IDs `EDU.BOOL.AND.v1`, `EDU.BOOL.OR.v1`, and `EDU.BOOL.XOR.v1`.

normativeRecords.exactText: For LAD/FBD value boxes, the registry exposes optional `EN:BOOL` and `ENO:BOOL`; omitted EN is TRUE. When EN is FALSE, the instruction does not read its formal input values or update state/effects, but independently scheduled upstream FBD nodes still execute. Pure value outputs and edge Q publish canonical defaults; timer Q/ET and counter Q/QU/QD/CV publish their stored last state-derived outputs; FILL, BLKMOVE, Boolean writes, and block calls perform no write/call; ENO is FALSE. On successful active execution ENO is TRUE. A runtime data fault performs no destination store, publishes ENO FALSE for the fault boundary, and then applies the profile's fatal policy. SCL intrinsic syntax does not expose EN/ENO and is always active when control reaches the call.

headingPath: 30. Phase 2 Verification and Implementation Exit Gate

normativeRecords.exactText: Journey A - complete authoring and run. From an empty project, use the production UI to add a fictional controller and digital/analog I/O, allocate addresses, create tags and a named structure, create FC/FB plus instance/global DB and scheduled OBs, author working logic, compile, preview/perform Virtual Download, enter RUN, change raw virtual inputs, observe deterministic outputs, monitor, watch, modify, force, trace, diagnose, save, close, and reopen without identity loss.

sourcePointer.documentPath: References for Codex from Scott/PLC Engineering Simulator - Codex Master Implementation Directive - Phase 2 of 4 - Runnable PLC Engineering Core.docx
headingPath: 30. Phase 2 Verification and Implementation Exit Gate

normativeRecords.exactText: Journey B - mixed language. A LAD OB calls supported FBD and SCL blocks. All three use one instruction registry, type system, compiler, typed IR, runtime, diagnostic model, and probe service. Equivalent fixtures produce equivalent observable values and events.

sourcePointer.documentPath: References for Codex from Scott/PLC Engineering Simulator - Codex Master Implementation Directive - Phase 2 of 4 - Runnable PLC Engineering Core.docx
headingPath: 30. Phase 2 Verification and Implementation Exit Gate

normativeRecords.exactText: Journey C - honest invalid engineering. Deliberate unresolved symbols, duplicate/overlapping addresses, stale FB interfaces, malformed LAD branches, illegal FBD wiring, SCL syntax/type errors, missing instances, and unsupported capability requests each produce genuine navigable diagnostics and no successful artifact. Repairing the underlying state clears the diagnostic through ordinary analysis.

sourcePointer.documentPath: References for Codex from Scott/PLC Engineering Simulator - Codex Master Implementation Directive - Phase 2 of 4 - Runnable PLC Engineering Core.docx
headingPath: 30. Phase 2 Verification and Implementation Exit Gate

normativeRecords.exactText: Journey D - identity and persistence. Rename preserves UUID references; delete leaves unresolved tombstones; undo restores the original UUID; copy assigns new UUIDs and remaps its closure; save/open/save preserves the graph; corrupt input fails without partial mutation.

sourcePointer.documentPath: References for Codex from Scott/PLC Engineering Simulator - Codex Master Implementation Directive - Phase 2 of 4 - Runnable PLC Engineering Core.docx
headingPath: 30. Phase 2 Verification and Implementation Exit Gate

normativeRecords.exactText: Journey E - runtime determinism. Process-image timing, timers, counters, FB state, faults, snapshot, restore, and replay are proven. Running the same build, snapshot, profile, seed, and ordered input/command sequence twice yields equivalent outputs, diagnostics, monitoring, and trace.

sourcePointer.documentPath: References for Codex from Scott/PLC Engineering Simulator - Codex Master Implementation Directive - Phase 2 of 4 - Runnable PLC Engineering Core.docx
headingPath: 30. Phase 2 Verification and Implementation Exit Gate

normativeRecords.exactText: Journey F - commissioning state separation. Invalid or stale work cannot load. Load preview exposes compatibility and initialization action. Atomic load rollback survives injected failure. Editing offline after load creates a visible mismatch; going online does not erase or synchronize it.

sourcePointer.documentPath: References for Codex from Scott/PLC Engineering Simulator - Codex Master Implementation Directive - Phase 2 of 4 - Runnable PLC Engineering Core.docx
headingPath: 30. Phase 2 Verification and Implementation Exit Gate

normativeRecords.exactText: Journey G - isolation counterfactual. Feed IPv4, IPv6, loopback, URL, hostname, protocol-looking, device-path, and malformed strings through every applicable virtual field and workflow while host adapters/devices are present and absent. Discovery results remain a subset of VirtualUniverse. The production process and attributable children/OS actions make zero external or physical attempt.

sourcePointer.documentPath: References for Codex from Scott/PLC Engineering Simulator - Codex Master Implementation Directive - Phase 2 of 4 - Runnable PLC Engineering Core.docx
headingPath: 30. Phase 2 Verification and Implementation Exit Gate

normativeRecords.exactText: Journey H - anti-theater mutations. Mutations that bypass the compiler, return canned diagnostics, script runtime outputs, hide active force, execute LAD by coordinates, create per-language runtime paths, accept an endpoint-like Virtual Download target, or add a production network/device API are detected by named tests and receive no credit through unrelated failure or crash.
